p: Treat The Victoria as the first stop on your Southend adventure. If you're arriving by train from London Liverpool Street, Southend Victoria station is right next door, and that makes it easy to pop in, pick up anything you need, then begin the walk down the High Street towards the sea. Southend Central station, on the line from Fenchurch Street, is also close to the High Street if you're coming that way.

Once you're at the seafront, the pier is the star of the show. Stretching well out into the Thames Estuary, it has its own little train to carry you out to the end, and there's a museum dedicated to its history at the shore end. Adventure Island, right beside the pier, is packed with rides for all ages, and the bright arcades along Marine Parade bring plenty of seaside buzz. Some arcade areas are 18+ only, so keep an eye out for signs if you've got kids with you.

For a change of scene, head west along the coast to Leigh-on-Sea. The cobbled streets of Old Leigh, with their cockle sheds and seafood stalls, have a lovely fishing village feel, and you can walk along the seafront through Chalkwell to get there. Hadleigh Castle, a romantic medieval ruin overlooking the estuary, is a little further on and well worth the effort for the views. Closer to the town centre, Prittlewell Priory is a historic museum set in peaceful parkland, which makes a good quiet escape from the crowds.
